code_snippet:
from kafka import KafkaConsumer
consumer = KafkaConsumer('orders', group_id='billing_app', bootstrap_servers=['localhost:9092'], enable_auto_commit=False)
for message in consumer:
    process_order(message.value)
    consumer.commit()  # Synchronous commit after successful processing

content.tldr: Kafka consumers retrieve records using a pull-based model, polling brokers for message batches and tracking progress via committed partition offsets.
content.simple_explanation: Kafka uses a pull-based consumer architecture instead of a push model. Consumers issue `poll()` calls to fetch batches of records from assigned partitions. This ensures consumers are never overwhelmed by high producer bursts, self-pacing based on local processing capacity. The consumer tracks its progress by committing an integer offset to the internal `__consumer_offsets` topic. If a consumer crashes, a replacement resumes reading from the last committed offset.
content.real_world_example: Reading chapters in an educational textbook: you place a physical bookmark at page 45; whenever you resume reading, you open directly to your bookmark rather than having someone read pages aloud at an overwhelming speed.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Enabling automatic offset commit (`enable_auto_commit=True`) commits offsets on a timer regardless of whether message processing succeeded, causing data loss during crashes. Critical systems must commit offsets manually after business logic succeeds.
